Summary: The greeting command: greet one another with a holy kiss, a warm and pure sign of fellowship. HELD ITEM, drafted on its merits: the borderline doubt is carried here, not resolved — the kiss itself is culturally conditioned and most churches greet differently.
Commandment: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
Application: The kiss was the ordinary warm greeting of the ancient world, made holy by the fellowship it expressed. The underlying warmth is clear; the form is the debate.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: to greet fellow believers with a warm, holy affection that marks them as one family.
Function: A warm greeting, made holy by the fellowship it expressed. This is an apostolic command, not Mosaic law, so the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it; the kiss itself is culturally conditioned, and most churches greet differently today. Its goal, on the TRADITIONAL reading, was to greet fellow believers with warm, holy affection that marks them as one family. The evil it addressed was coldness between brethren — a family that does not greet as family. It restrained that evil by commanding the greeting itself: greet one another with a holy kiss.
